title: Powerdevil should call logind SetIdleHint on user idle
line: Plasma now tells logind when you are away, so other programs can see that the session is idle.
explanation: Nothing in Plasma ever called SetIdleHint on the logind (or ConsoleKit) session, so its IdleHint stayed false forever and tools like Clight, which follow it to pause their work, never saw the user go idle. Powerdevil already holds the session object in its policy agent but only used it for inhibitions. Méven's MR !699 adds a small bundled action that sets the hint to true after SessionIdleTimeoutSec without input (powerdevilrc General, default 300 s, 0 = never) and back to false on activity, re-sends it if logind restarts, and adds 'idle' to the block lock PowerDevil already takes so logind's own IdleAction= doesn't run on top of PowerDevil's timeouts.

commits.message:
daemon: Report the idle state of the session with SetIdleHint

Nothing in Plasma told logind or ConsoleKit that the session was idle,
so tools like Clight never saw IdleHint change. A new action now sets it
after SessionIdleTimeoutSec without input, and logind's idle is blocked.

BUG: 448942

media.caption: Master: the session's IdleHint stays false through 40 s without input (idle timeout set to 10 s).
With the MR: IdleHint turns true 10 s after the last input and false again as soon as the pointer moves.
Master: 24 s idle, then a pointer move; IdleHint never changes.
With the MR: idle for 16 s, IdleHint goes true, then false on the pointer move.
